1.w: And the Pharisees and some of the scribes having come from Jerusalem are gathered together to Him.

2.w: And they had seen some of His disciples, that with defiled hands—that is, unwashed—they are eating the loaves.

3.w: (For the Pharisees and all the Jews do not eat unless they wash the hands to the fist, holding to the tradition of the elders;

4.w: and [coming] from the marketplace, they do not eat unless they immerse; and there are many other things that they received to hold to—immersions of cups and pitchers and bronze vessels and couches.)

5.w: And the Pharisees and the scribes questioned Him, “Why do Your disciples not walk according to the tradition of the elders, but eat the bread with defiled hands?”

6.w: And He said to them, “Isaiah prophesied correctly about you⁺ hypocrites, as it has been written: ‘This people honors Me with the lips, but their heart is kept far away from Me;

7.w: and in vain they worship Me, teaching [as] teachings the precepts of men.’

8.w: Having left the commandment of God, you⁺ hold to the tradition of men.”

9.w: And He was saying to them, “Nobly do you⁺ set aside the commandment of God so that you⁺ might keep your⁺ tradition.

10.w: For Moses said, ‘Honor your father and your mother,’ and, ‘The one speaking evil of father or mother, in death let him end.’

11.w: But you⁺ say [that] if a man might say to the father or to the mother, ‘Whatever you might be profited from me [is] Corban’ (that is, a gift),

12.w: no longer do you⁺ permit him to do anything for the father or for the mother,

13.w: making void the word of God for your⁺ tradition, which you⁺ delivered. And you⁺ do many things as such.”

14.w: And having summoned the crowd again, He was saying to them, “Hear Me, all, and understand:

15.w: There is nothing from outside the man entering into him that is able to defile him; but the things proceeding out of the man are the things defiling the man.”

17.w: And when He entered into the house from the crowd, His disciples were questioning Him [about] the parable.

18.w: And He says to them, “Thus are you⁺ also without understanding? Do you⁺ not understand that everything entering into the man from outside is not able to defile him,

19.w: because it does not enter into his heart, but into the belly, and goes out into the sewer?”—[thus] purifying all the foods.

20.w: And He was saying, “That which is proceeding out of the man, that defiles the man.

21.w: For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil reasonings, sexual immorality, thefts, murders, adulteries,

22.w: covetous desires, wickednesses, deceit, sensuality, an evil eye, slander, pride, foolishness.

23.w: All these evils proceed from within, and they defile the man.”

24.w: And from there having risen up, He went away into the borders of Tyre. And having entered into a house, He was wanting no one to know [it], and He was not able to be hidden.

25.w: But immediately, having heard about Him, a woman whose little daughter had an unclean spirit, having come, fell at His feet.

26.w: Now the woman was a Greek, Syrophoenician by race, and she was asking Him that He might cast the demon out of her daughter.

27.w: And He was saying to her, “Permit the children first to be satisfied; for it is not good to take the bread of the children and to cast [it] to the dogs.”

28.w: But she answered, and she says to Him, “Yes, Lord, even the dogs under the table eat from the crumbs of the children.”

29.w: And He said to her, “Because of this word, go; the demon has gone forth out of your daughter.”

30.w: And having gone away to her house, she found the child laid on the bed, and the demon having gone out.

31.w: And again, having gone out from the borders of Tyre, He went through Sidon to the Sea of Galilee, through the midst of the borders of the Decapolis.

32.w: And they bring to Him a deaf [man] (and he spoke with difficulty), and they implore Him that He might lay the hand on him.

33.w: And having taken him away from the crowd by himself, He put His fingers into his ears. And having spit, He touched his tongue.

34.w: And having looked up to heaven, He sighed deeply, and He says to him, “Ephphatha!” (that is, “Be opened!”)

35.w: And his ears were opened, and immediately the band of his tongue was loosed, and he was speaking rightly.

36.w: And He instructed them that they should tell no one. But as much as He was instructing them, they were proclaiming [it] more abundantly.

37.w: And they were astonished above measure, saying, “He has done all things well! He makes both the deaf to hear and the mute to speak!”
